name: prometheus.rules

tmpl_string.description: A string which is template-expanded before usage.

record.description: The name of the time series to output to. Must be a valid metric name.

expr.description: The PromQL expression to evaluate. Every evaluation cycle this is evaluated at the current time, and the result recorded as a new set of time series with the metric name as given by 'record'.

labels.description: Labels to add or overwrite before storing the result.

alert.description: The name of the alert. Must be a valid metric name.

expr.description: The PromQL expression to evaluate. Every evaluation cycle this is evaluated at the current time, and all resultant time series become pending/firing alerts.

for.description: Alerts are considered firing once they have been returned for this long. Alerts which have not yet fired for long enough are considered pending.

keep_firing_for.description: How long an alert will continue firing after the condition that triggered it has cleared.

labels.description: Labels to add or overwrite for each alert.

annotations.description: Annotations to add to each alert.

name.description: The name of the group. Must be unique within a file.

interval.description: How often rules in the group are evaluated.

labels.description: Labels to add or overwrite before storing the result for its rules. Labels defined in <rule> will override the key if it has a collision.

limit.description: Limit the number of alerts an alerting rule and series a recording rule can produce. 0 is no limit.

description:
The Prometheus rule file defines a single group called **example_group**, which is evaluated every 1 minute. This group carries the labels **environment=production** and **team=backend**, and it imposes no limit on the number of alerts or series generated (limit = 0).  

Within the group there are two rules. The first is a recording rule named **node_cpu_seconds_total:rate5m** that records the expression `rate(node_cpu_seconds_total[5m])` and adds the label **job=node** to the resulting series. The second is an alerting rule called **HighCPUUsage**; it fires when the metric `node_cpu_seconds_total{mode="system"}` exceeds 80. The alert must remain true for **2 minutes** before it becomes active, and once triggered it will keep firing for **10 minutes** after the condition clears. This alert is tagged with the label **severity=critical** and includes two annotations: a summary – “CPU usage is high on {{ $labels.instance }}” – and a description – “The CPU usage has exceeded 80% for more than 2 minutes.”

annotations.description: The CPU usage has exceeded 80% for more than 2 minutes.
